statusMeaning.implemented: Behaviour ported and reachable in the UI; covered by tests, but not every upstream test case has a ported equivalent.
statusMeaning.verified: Additionally, the upstream test cases of the area have ported equivalents that pass (unit and/or browser e2e).
statusMeaning.in_progress: Implemented, but a required target (e.g. performance) is not met yet.

deviations: Browsers reserve ⌘N/⌘W: ⌥⌘N/⌥⌘W in a browser, ⌘N/⌘W as aliases where a host passes them on.
Page close offers only the browser's generic prompt; per-tab Save/Don't Save happens when closing a tab. IndexedDB recovery copies cover reloads and crashes.
Non-separable blend modes stacked on each other can differ by isolated large values between GPU and CPU where SetSat is discontinuous (statistical bound in gpu-vs-cpu).

Without WebGL 2 a CPU/Canvas 2D renderer takes over (tests/e2e/software-render.spec.ts): same compositing semantics via the CPU compositor, view-resolution rendering with a mip cache; it is slower than the GPU path, and first views of large layers take longer while mips are built.
Layer textures are sparse chunks with 64 px aprons instead of TiledLayerRenderer pieces; readback is full resolution beyond MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE.
Core Image perspective sampling is replaced by inverse homography with premultiplied bilinear sampling.
The system clipboard is read through the paste event or the async Clipboard API; after a denied permission only the internal clipboard is available.
Large soft brushes use a two-pixel quadratic density reconstruction (≤1/255 against the reference implementation).

During a stroke, paint/erase on layers and masks is previewed by GPU coverage (MetalBrushCoverage port, ≤2/255 against the exact CPU result); the exact raster is computed incrementally in a Web Worker and committed about 0.25 s after pointer-up as one undo step. Clone Stamp, Spot Healing, Smudge/Blur and selection-limited strokes keep the synchronous CPU preview.

Gaussian Blur is a normalized Gaussian (σ = radius, ±3σ, premultiplied sRGB), recursive Young–van Vliet for large radii (≤1/255 vs direct convolution); Motion Blur is a Gaussian-weighted directional line integral with bilinear sampling. Core Image's proprietary kernels and rounding cannot be reproduced bit-exactly.
Blur previews keep the original layer grid; Apply uses the expanded bounds as upstream.

Apple Vision is replaced by two local models on ONNX Runtime Web (WebGPU or WASM): U²-Netp (Apache-2.0, 4.6 MB, bundled, 'Fast') and BiRefNet_lite (MIT, 200 MB, downloaded once and cached, 'Best quality', host can self-host via subjectModelUrls).
Vision's separate subject instances are approximated by connected components of the mask; all foreground components are kept, as upstream keeps all foreground subjects.
Best quality on WASM (no WebGPU) is slow (≈36 s for a 1456×816 photo on the reference CPU) and needs ≈3 GB peak memory.
Browser tests with the real models need reference photos / the downloaded model outside the repository and are skipped when absent.

evidence: tests/e2e/own-files.spec.ts (integrator files: AdobeRGB/ECI/ProPhoto16/CMYK TIFF+JPEG, camera HEIC)
deviations: HEIC: decoded by the browser where supported (Safari); otherwise by an optional host codec (planned Tauri app: OS codecs, see docs/tauri-heic.md), or by the opt-in LGPL-3.0 libheif/libde265 WASM module (off by default; HEVC patents are the distributor's responsibility); else a readable error.

Colour: embedded ICC profiles are converted to sRGB with Little CMS 2 (MIT, WASM) for PNG (iCCP, cHRM/gAMA, sRGB), TIFF (tag 34675) and tagged JPEG (decoded with libjpeg-turbo, IJG/BSD, incl. Adobe CMYK/YCCK), identical in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; untagged JPEGs use the browser decoder; untagged CMYK uses a generic subtractive profile; the libheif path applies NCLX but not arbitrary embedded ICC profiles.
Default project format is the host contract's ZIP archive; the macOS .comp package (versions 1–7) is read (zipped or as a folder) and written as a copy.
Save overwrites a chosen file only where the File System Access API exists (Chromium); other browsers download.
